title: Bradley's nightclub across the Pearl River
summary: Playing at Bradley's for fifty cents a night plus tips, learning to hear and make up tunes without written music.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: And I also played at a place across the Pearl(?) River, the famous or ill-famed Pearl River, at a place called Bradley's with Doc Palmer. It was like... It had a filling station out in front, and a grocery store, and then a nightclub in the back. And we played in the nightclub part. And our basic salary was three dollars and fifty cents a week, seven nights -- we were making 50 cents a night actually in salary. And the rest we would make in tips. That was the thing, people tipping. And that was quite an experience. [BARELY AUDIBLE] We'd get all these requests,

and we'd make up our own tunes; you know, you had to learn from scratch... And it was a little band, and we didn't read any music, so that helped me with my ear things -- learning to hear and make things happen.
